questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reactions is preferentially used to prepare the corresponding paraffins from alkanone?
questions.solution:
Alkanones (ketones) are reduced to the corresponding paraffins (alkanes) by Clemmensen reduction. In this reaction, the carbonyl group ($\gt C=O$) is converted into a methylene group ($\gt CH_2$) using zinc amalgam ($Zn-Hg$) and concentrated hydrochloric acid ($HCl$).

Etard reaction is used to oxidize toluene to benzaldehyde.

Rosenmund reduction is used to convert acid chlorides into aldehydes.

Haloform reaction is used to convert methyl ketones into a haloform and a carboxylic acid salt.

Answer: Clemmensen reduction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds exhibits Schiff test?
questions.solution:
Schiff's reagent is a dilute solution of rosaniline hydrochloride (magenta dye) whose pink colour has been discharged by passing $SO_2$.

When an aldehyde is treated with Schiff's reagent, the pink or magenta colour is restored.

Ketones, carboxylic acids, and ethers do not respond to this test.

Therefore, aldehydes exhibit the Schiff test.

Answer: Aldehydes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reaction represents Rosenmund reduction ?
questions.solution:
Rosenmund reduction is the catalytic hydrogenation of an acid chloride to an aldehyde.

The catalyst used is palladium on barium sulfate ($\text{Pd}-\text{BaSO}_4$), which is partially poisoned to prevent further reduction of the aldehyde to an alcohol.

The reaction is given by:
$\text{R}-\text{CO}-\text{Cl} \xrightarrow[\text{Pd}-\text{BaSO}_4]{\text{H}_2} \text{R}-\text{CHO} + \text{HCl}$

The other reactions are:
Stephen reaction: Reduction of nitriles to aldehydes using $\text{SnCl}_2/\text{HCl}$ followed by hydrolysis.
Clemmensen reduction: Reduction of aldehydes or ketones to alkanes using $\text{Zn}-\text{Hg}$ and conc. $\text{HCl}$.
Wolff-Kishner reduction: Reduction of aldehydes or ketones to alkanes using hydrazine and a strong base like $\text{KOH}$ in ethylene glycol.

Answer: $\text{R}-\text{CO}-\text{Cl} \xrightarrow[\large{\text{Pd}-\text{BaSO}_4}]{\large{\text{H}_2}} \text{R}-\text{CHO} + \text{HCl}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the product formed on Rosenmund reduction of benzoyl chloride ?
questions.solution:
Rosenmund reduction is the catalytic hydrogenation of an acid chloride to an aldehyde.

The reagent used is hydrogen gas in the presence of a palladium catalyst supported on barium sulfate ($H_2 / Pd-BaSO_4$).

When benzoyl chloride ($C_6H_5COCl$) is subjected to Rosenmund reduction, it is reduced to benzaldehyde ($C_6H_5CHO$).

The reaction is:
$C_6H_5COCl + H_2 \xrightarrow{Pd/BaSO_4} C_6H_5CHO + HCl$

Therefore, the product formed is benzaldehyde.

Answer: Benzaldehyde

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the 'product' in the following reaction.
Pent - 3 - enenitrile $\xrightarrow[\large{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+}]{\large{\text{Al H (i-Bu)}_2}}$ Product
questions.solution:
The given reactant is pent-3-enenitrile, which has the structure $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CN}$.

Diisobutylaluminium hydride (DIBAL-H), represented as $\text{AlH(i-Bu)}_2$, is a selective reducing agent. It reduces nitriles to imines at low temperatures, which upon subsequent acidic hydrolysis ($\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$) yield aldehydes.

DIBAL-H does not reduce isolated carbon-carbon double bonds.

The reaction proceeds as follows:
$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}\equiv\text{N} \xrightarrow{\text{AlH(i-Bu)}_2} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{N}-\text{Al(i-Bu)}_2$

$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{N}-\text{Al(i-Bu)}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHO}$

The final product is pent-3-enal.

Answer: Pent - 3 - enal

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Propyne on reaction with water in presence of $40\%$ sulphuric acid and $1\%$ mercuric sulphate forms
questions.solution:
Propyne undergoes hydration in the presence of dilute sulphuric acid and mercuric sulphate according to Markovnikov's rule.

The addition of a water molecule to the triple bond initially yields an unstable enol intermediate, prop-1-en-2-ol.

$CH_3-C \equiv CH + H_2O \xrightarrow{Hg^{2+}, H^+} CH_3-C(OH)=CH_2$

The enol intermediate rapidly undergoes tautomerization to form the more stable keto form, propanone.

$CH_3-C(OH)=CH_2 \rightleftharpoons CH_3-CO-CH_3$

Answer: Propanone

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Benzonitrile on reaction with a reagent in dry ether followed by hydrolysis forms benzophenone along with ammonia and hydroxymagnesium bromide. Identify the reagent used in above transformation.
questions.solution:
Benzonitrile ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CN}$) reacts with a Grignard reagent to form an imine salt, which on hydrolysis gives a ketone.

Since the product is benzophenone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COC}_6\text{H}_5$), the Grignard reagent must provide a phenyl group ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5^-$).

The formation of hydroxymagnesium bromide ($\text{Mg(OH)Br}$) as a by-product indicates that the halogen in the Grignard reagent is bromine.

The reaction is:

$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CN} + \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{MgBr} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} (\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)_2\text{C=NMgBr}$

$(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)_2\text{C=NMgBr} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow (\text{C}_6\text{H}_5)_2\text{C=O} + \text{NH}_3 + \text{Mg(OH)Br}$

The reagent used is $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{MgBr}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the product 'B' in the following reaction
$\text{Isopropyl cyanide} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{SnCl}_2, \text{HCl}}} \text{A} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+}} \text{B} + \text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$
questions.solution:
The given reaction is Stephen reduction.

Isopropyl cyanide is $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CN}$.

When isopropyl cyanide is treated with $\text{SnCl}_2$ and $\text{HCl}$, it undergoes reduction to form an imine hydrochloride intermediate (A).

$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CN} + 2[\text{H}] + \text{HCl} \xrightarrow{\text{SnCl}_2, \text{HCl}} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}=\text{NH}\cdot\text{HCl}$ (A)

Acidic hydrolysis of the imine hydrochloride yields the corresponding aldehyde (B).

$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}=\text{NH}\cdot\text{HCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CHO} + \text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$

The product B is $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CHO}$, which is 2-methylpropanal.

Answer: 2-Methylpropanal

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the reagent 'R' used in the following reaction
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCl} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{R}}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO} + \text{HCl}$
questions.solution:
The given reaction is the conversion of benzoyl chloride ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCl}$) to benzaldehyde ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$).

This transformation is known as the Rosenmund reduction.

The reagent used for this reaction is hydrogen gas in the presence of a palladium catalyst supported on barium sulfate ($\text{H}_2, \text{Pd}-\text{BaSO}_4$).

The barium sulfate acts as a catalytic poison that partially deactivates the palladium, preventing the further reduction of the newly formed aldehyde into an alcohol.

Thus, the reagent 'R' is $\text{H}_2, \text{Pd}-\text{BaSO}_4$.

Answer: $\text{H}_2, \text{Pd}-\text{BaSO}_4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product 'Y' in the following reaction $\text{Benzonitrile} \xrightarrow{\large{\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{MgBr} / \text{dry ether}}} X \xrightarrow{\large{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+}} Y + \text{MgBr(OH)} + \text{NH}_3$
questions.solution:
Benzonitrile is $C_6H_5CN$.

When benzonitrile reacts with phenylmagnesium bromide ($C_6H_5MgBr$) in the presence of dry ether, a nucleophilic addition takes place at the electrophilic carbon of the cyanide group, forming an imine salt intermediate ($X$).

$C_6H_5CN + C_6H_5MgBr \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} (C_6H_5)_2C=NMgBr$

Upon acid hydrolysis ($H_3O^+$), the imine salt intermediate ($X$) is converted into a ketone.

$(C_6H_5)_2C=NMgBr \xrightarrow{H_3O^+} (C_6H_5)_2C=O + NH_3 + MgBr(OH)$

The product $Y$ is $(C_6H_5)_2C=O$, which is benzophenone.

Answer: Benzophenone

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the name of the above reaction.
questions.solution:
The given reaction shows the conversion of benzene to benzaldehyde using carbon monoxide ($CO$) and hydrogen chloride ($HCl$) in the presence of anhydrous aluminum chloride ($AlCl_3$) under high pressure.

This specific transformation is known as the Gatterman-Koch formylation reaction. In this reaction, a formyl cation is generated in situ from $CO$, $HCl$, and the Lewis acid catalyst ($AlCl_3$), which then undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution with benzene to form benzaldehyde.

Let us review the other options:
1. Etard reaction: Involves the oxidation of toluene to benzaldehyde using chromyl chloride ($CrO_2Cl_2$).
2. Stephen reaction: Involves the reduction of nitriles to aldehydes using tin(II) chloride ($SnCl_2$) and $HCl$, followed by hydrolysis.
3. Rosenmund reaction: Involves the catalytic hydrogenation of acid chlorides to aldehydes using palladium on barium sulfate ($Pd/BaSO_4$).

Therefore, the correct name for the given reaction is the Gatterman-Koch formylation reaction.

Answer: Gatterman-Koch formylation reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Acetone on heating with $\text{CrO}_3$ mainly forms,
questions.solution:
Ketones are generally resistant to oxidation under normal conditions. However, on vigorous heating with strong oxidizing agents like $\text{CrO}_3$, they undergo cleavage of the C-C bond to form carboxylic acids with fewer carbon atoms.

Acetone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$) undergoes oxidation to form a two-carbon carboxylic acid and a one-carbon fragment which further oxidizes to carbon dioxide and water.

$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{CrO}_3, \Delta} \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

The main product formed is acetic acid.

Answer: Acetic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An organic compound $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH=CH-CH}_2\text{-CHO}$ is taken in two different containers A and B. Sample in A is treated with $\text{H}_2$ / Ni forming new compound P. Sample in B is treated with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ and hydrolyzed further forming new compound Q. Identify P and Q.
questions.solution:
The given organic compound is $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH=CH-CH}_2\text{-CHO}$.

When treated with $\text{H}_2$ in the presence of Ni catalyst, both the carbon-carbon double bond and the aldehyde group are reduced. The alkene is reduced to an alkane and the aldehyde is reduced to a primary alcohol. Thus, the product P is pentan-1-ol, which is $\text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$.

When treated with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ followed by hydrolysis, only the aldehyde group is reduced to a primary alcohol. $\text{LiAlH}_4$ does not reduce isolated carbon-carbon double bonds. Thus, the double bond remains intact and the product Q is pent-3-en-1-ol, which is $\text{CH}_3\text{-CH=CH-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$.

Therefore, $\text{P} = \text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ and $\text{Q} = \text{CH}_3\text{-CH=CH-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$.

Answer: $\text{P} = \text{CH}_3(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ and $\text{Q} = \text{CH}_3\text{-CH=CH-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of following observations is found in Tollens test for aldehydes?
options: The formation of pink or magenta color upon the addition of the reagent to the sample solution.
Formation of an Ag layer on sides of test tube upon addition and warming of the reagent.
Formation of brick-red precipitate upon heating with reagent.
Appearance of red color upon shaking with reagent.
questions.solution:
Tollens' reagent is an ammoniacal silver nitrate solution, $[Ag(NH_3)_2]^+$.

When an aldehyde is warmed with Tollens' reagent, the aldehyde is oxidized to the corresponding carboxylate ion, while the silver ions are reduced to metallic silver.

$RCHO + 2[Ag(NH_3)_2]^+ + 3OH^- \rightarrow RCOO^- + 2Ag\downarrow + 4NH_3 + 2H_2O$

The metallic silver deposits on the inner walls of the test tube, forming a characteristic silver mirror or an Ag layer. This observation confirms the presence of an aldehyde group.

The formation of a pink or magenta color is observed in Schiff's test, and a brick-red precipitate is observed in Fehling's test.

Answer: Formation of an Ag layer on sides of test tube upon addition and warming of the reagent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Aldehydes are more reactive than ketone towards nucleophilic attack because of?
options: presence of two alkyl group on ketone decreases its electrophilicity
presence of one alkyl group on aldehyde decreases its electrophilicity
alkyl group have electron withdrawing effect.
questions.solution:
The reactivity of carbonyl compounds towards nucleophilic addition depends on steric and electronic factors.

Steric factor: Ketones have two alkyl groups attached to the carbonyl carbon, which causes more steric hindrance to the approaching nucleophile compared to aldehydes, which have only one alkyl group and one small hydrogen atom.

Electronic factor: Alkyl groups are electron-donating in nature due to the $+I$ effect. In ketones, the presence of two electron-donating alkyl groups reduces the partial positive charge on the carbonyl carbon more effectively than the single alkyl group in aldehydes. This decreases the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon in ketones, making them less reactive towards nucleophilic attack.

Therefore, the presence of two alkyl groups on a ketone decreases its electrophilicity.

Answer: presence of two alkyl group on ketone decreases its electrophilicity

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is true regarding Cannizzaro reaction?
options: Some aldehydes are converted to the respective alcohols and the salt of the respective carboxylic acid.
Primary amine is converted into isocyanide
questions.solution:
Cannizzaro reaction is a disproportionation reaction in which aldehydes without an $\alpha$-hydrogen atom are treated with a strong base.

In this reaction, one molecule of the aldehyde is reduced to the corresponding primary alcohol, while another molecule is oxidized to the salt of the corresponding carboxylic acid.

For example, formaldehyde ($HCHO$) reacts with concentrated $NaOH$ to form methanol ($CH_3OH$) and sodium formate ($HCOONa$).

Therefore, some aldehydes are converted to the respective alcohols and the salt of the respective carboxylic acid.

Answer: Some aldehydes are converted to the respective alcohols and the salt of the respective carboxylic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds can not form iodoform?
questions.solution:
The iodoform test is given by compounds containing either a methyl ketone group ($CH_3-CO-$) or a secondary alcohol group with a terminal methyl ($CH_3-CH(OH)-$ group), as well as ethanol and acetaldehyde.

Ethyl methyl ketone ($CH_3-CO-CH_2-CH_3$) contains a $CH_3-CO-$ group, so it gives a positive iodoform test.

Isopropyl alcohol ($CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_3$) contains a $CH_3-CH(OH)-$ group, so it gives a positive iodoform test.

3-Methyl-2-butanone ($CH_3-CO-CH(CH_3)_2$) contains a $CH_3-CO-$ group, so it gives a positive iodoform test.

Isobutyl alcohol ($(CH_3)_2CH-CH_2-OH$) is a primary alcohol (other than ethanol) and does not contain a $CH_3-CH(OH)-$ group. Upon oxidation, it forms isobutyraldehyde, which lacks a $CH_3-CO-$ group. Therefore, it does not give the iodoform test.

Answer: Isobutyl alcohol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds dose NOT respond positively to the iodoform test ?
questions.solution:
The iodoform test is given by compounds containing a methyl ketone group ($CH_3-CO-$) or a secondary alcohol group with a terminal methyl ($CH_3-CH(OH)-$), which gets oxidized to a methyl ketone by the reagent.

Acetaldehyde ($CH_3-CHO$) contains a $CH_3-CO-$ group and gives a positive test.

Propan-2-ol ($CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_3$) contains a $CH_3-CH(OH)-$ group and gives a positive test.

Propanone ($CH_3-CO-CH_3$) contains a $CH_3-CO-$ group and gives a positive test.

Pentan-3-one ($CH_3-CH_2-CO-CH_2-CH_3$) does not contain a $CH_3-CO-$ group. Therefore, it does not respond positively to the iodoform test.

Answer: Pentan-3-one

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product obtained when ketone reacts with $\text{NH}_2$-$\text{NH}_2$.
questions.solution:
Ketones react with hydrazine ($H_2N-NH_2$) to form hydrazones.

The reaction proceeds via nucleophilic addition of hydrazine to the carbonyl group, followed by the elimination of a water molecule.

$R_2C=O + H_2N-NH_2 \rightarrow R_2C=N-NH_2 + H_2O$

The resulting product, $R_2C=N-NH_2$, is known as a hydrazone.

Answer: Hydrazone

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the reagent used in the transformation of Ketone into semicarbazone.
questions.solution:
The transformation of a ketone into a semicarbazone involves the reaction of the ketone with semicarbazide.

The chemical formula of semicarbazide is $\text{NH}_2-\text{NH}-\text{CONH}_2$.

The reaction proceeds via nucleophilic addition followed by the elimination of a water molecule, resulting in the formation of a semicarbazone ($\gt \text{C}=\text{N}-\text{NH}-\text{CONH}_2$).

Other reagents given:
$\text{NH}_2-\text{OH}$ (hydroxylamine) forms an oxime.
$\text{NH}_2-\text{NH}_2$ (hydrazine) forms a hydrazone.
$\text{NH}_2-\text{NH}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$ (phenylhydrazine) forms a phenylhydrazone.

Answer: $\text{NH}_2-\text{NH}-\text{CONH}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When ethanal and propanal undergo aldol condensation with dilute NaOH, the pair of products obtained by cross condensation reaction is
questions.solution:
Ethanal is $CH_3CHO$ and propanal is $CH_3CH_2CHO$.

Cross aldol condensation occurs when the enolate ion of one aldehyde attacks the carbonyl carbon of the other aldehyde.

Case 1: Enolate of ethanal attacks propanal.
$CH_3CH_2CHO + CH_3CHO \xrightarrow{OH^-} CH_3CH_2CH(OH)CH_2CHO \xrightarrow{\Delta} CH_3CH_2CH=CHCHO$
The product formed is pent-2-enal.

Case 2: Enolate of propanal attacks ethanal.
$CH_3CHO + CH_3CH_2CHO \xrightarrow{OH^-} CH_3CH(OH)CH(CH_3)CHO \xrightarrow{\Delta} CH_3CH=C(CH_3)CHO$
The product formed is 2-methylbut-2-enal.

Thus, the pair of products obtained by cross condensation is 2-methylbut-2-enal and pent-2-enal.

Answer: 2-methylbut-2-enal and pent-2-enal

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In Gatterman reaction, which of the following catalyst is used?
questions.solution:
The Gatterman reaction is a modification of the Sandmeyer reaction used for the synthesis of aryl halides from aryl diazonium salts. In this reaction, finely divided copper powder is used as a catalyst along with a halogen acid such as $\text{HCl}$ or $\text{HBr}$.

$\text{Ar-N}_2^+ \text{X}^- \xrightarrow{\text{Cu powder / HX}} \text{Ar-X} + \text{N}_2$

Option (318007) represents the reagents for the Gatterman-Koch formylation reaction.

Option (318010) represents the reagents for the Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction.

Therefore, copper powder and $\text{HBr}$ are used in the Gatterman reaction.

Answer: Copper powder and HBr

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product obtained when Grignard reagent reacts with alkyl cyanide followed by acid hydrolysis.
questions.solution:
Grignard reagents ($R'MgX$) react with alkyl cyanides ($R-C\equiv N$) to form an imine salt intermediate.

$R-C\equiv N + R'MgX \rightarrow R-C(R')=NMgX$

Upon acid hydrolysis, the imine salt is converted into a ketone.

$R-C(R')=NMgX + H_3O^+ \rightarrow R-C(=O)-R' + NH_3 + Mg(OH)X$

Thus, the final product obtained is a ketone.

Answer: a ketone

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Acetaldehyde, when heated in the presence of sodium hydroxide and iodine forms
questions.solution:
Acetaldehyde ($CH_3CHO$) contains a $CH_3-CO-$ group, so it undergoes the iodoform reaction when heated with iodine and sodium hydroxide.

The reaction proceeds as follows:

$CH_3CHO + 3I_2 + 4NaOH \xrightarrow{\Delta} CHI_3 + HCOONa + 3NaI + 3H_2O$

The products formed are iodoform ($CHI_3$) as a yellow precipitate and sodium formate ($HCOONa$).

Answer: Sodium formate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reactions is an example of a disproportionation reaction?
questions.solution:
A disproportionation reaction is a redox reaction in which the same substance undergoes both oxidation and reduction simultaneously.

In the Cannizzaro reaction, aldehydes lacking $\alpha$-hydrogens undergo self-oxidation and self-reduction in the presence of a concentrated base.

One molecule of the aldehyde is reduced to the corresponding alcohol, while another molecule is oxidized to the salt of the corresponding carboxylic acid.

For example: $2HCHO + NaOH \rightarrow HCOONa + CH_3OH$

Here, formaldehyde is oxidized to sodium formate and reduced to methanol. Thus, the Cannizzaro reaction is an example of a disproportionation reaction.

Wolf-Kishner and Clemmensen reductions are purely reduction reactions, whereas Aldol condensation is a condensation reaction.

Answer: Cannizzaro reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the reagent used for Rosenmund reduction.
questions.solution:
The Rosenmund reduction selectively converts acyl chlorides to aldehydes using hydrogen gas over palladium on barium sulfate ($\mathrm{H}_2 / \mathrm{Pd}, \mathrm{BaSO}_4$). The barium sulfate serves as a catalyst poison, moderating the palladium's activity to prevent over-reduction to the alcohol.

$\mathrm{H}_2 / \mathrm{Ni}$ is a standard hydrogenation catalyst, while $\mathrm{Na}-\mathrm{Hg} / \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ and $\mathrm{SnCl}_2-\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ are unrelated, being employed in other reduction mechanisms.

The correct choice is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the reaction so that carbonyl group of aldehydes and ketones is reduced to methylene group on treatment with Zinc-amalgam and concentrated hydrochloric acid.
questions.solution:
The reaction characterized by reduction of a carbonyl group to a methylene group using zinc–amalgam and concentrated $\mathrm{HCl}$ is known as the Clemmensen reduction.

In comparison, the Wolf–Kishner reduction employs hydrazine and a strong base such as $\mathrm{KOH}$ or $\mathrm{NaOH}\;$, the Stephan reaction converts nitriles to aldehydes using stannous chloride and hydrochloric acid followed by hydrolysis, while the Étard reaction oxidizes a methyl group attached to an aromatic ring to an aldehyde using chromyl chloride.

The correct answer is $\boxed{C}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following has higher boiling point?
questions.solution:
Boiling points in a homologous series depend primarily on molecular weight and the resulting London dispersion forces. All aldehydes exhibit dipole-dipole interactions but cannot form intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

Molecular weights increase as follows: ethanal (2 carbons), propanal (3 carbons), pentanal (5 carbons), hexanal (6 carbons). With increasing molecular weight, surface area and dispersion forces strengthen, requiring more energy to vaporize.

Hexanal has the highest molecular weight and thus the strongest intermolecular forces, resulting in the highest boiling point.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product formed when Hex-3-enenitrile is reduced with diisobutylaluminium hydride followed by acid hydrolysis?
questions.solution:
Structure identification: Hex-3-ennenitrile corresponds to $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH=CH-CH_2-CN}$. Reduction with DIBAL-H selectively reduces the nitrile to an imine without affecting the isolated alkene: $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH=CH-CH_2-CN \xrightarrow{DIBAL-H} CH_3-CH_2-CH=CH-CH_2-CH=NH}$. Acid hydrolysis converts the imine to the aldehyde: $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH=CH-CH_2-CH=NH \xrightarrow{H_3 O^+} CH_3-CH_2-CH=CH-CH_2-CHO + NH_3}$. The product $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH=CH-CH_2-CHO}$ is hex-3-enal. Option comparison:
A: Hexanal ($\mathrm{CH_3(CH_2)_4CHO}$, saturated)
B: Hexan-3-one ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COCH_2CH_2CH_3}$, ketone)
C: Hex-3-enal (matches product)
D: Hexanoic acid ($\mathrm{CH_3(CH_2)_4COOH}$, carboxylic acid)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the products of following reaction?
$\text { Formaldehyde }+ \text { Benzaldehyde } \xrightarrow[\text { ii) } \mathrm{H}_3 \mathrm{O}^{+}]{\text {i) conc. } \mathrm{NaOH}} \text { Products }$
questions.solution:
Crossed Cannizzaro Reaction of Formaldehyde and Benzaldehyde

Formaldehyde ($\mathrm{HCHO}$) and benzaldehyde ($\mathrm{C_6 H_5CHO}$) are both aldehydes lacking alpha-hydrogens, qualifying them for the Cannizzaro reaction. In crossed Cannizzaro reactions, formaldehyde is preferentially oxidized due to its greater reactivity, while the partner aldehyde is reduced.

Concentrated $\mathrm{NaOH}$ initiates hydride transfer: formaldehyde is oxidized to formate ion ($\mathrm{HCOO^-}$), which upon acidification yields methanoic acid ($\mathrm{HCOOH}$). Benzaldehyde is reduced to benzyl alkoxide ($\mathrm{C_6 H_5CH_2 O-}$), producing phenylmethanol ($\mathrm{C_6 H_5CH_2 OH}$) after acid workup.

$\mathrm{HCHO}$ oxidizes to $\mathrm{HCOOH}$, while $\mathrm{C_6 H_5CHO}$ reduces to $\mathrm{C_6 H_5CH_2 OH}$.

The products are methanoic acid and phenylmethanol, corresponding to option C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following does NOT exhibit haloform reaction?
questions.solution:
Haloform Reaction Analysis

Compounds exhibiting the haloform reaction contain the methyl ketone group $CH_3CO-$ or are oxidizable to this structure (e.g., $CH_3CH(OH)R$).

Ethanal ($CH_3CHO$) contains the $CH_3CO-$ moiety and undergoes haloform reaction.

Propanone ($CH_3COCH_3$) is a methyl ketone with two $CH_3CO-$ groups and exhibits the reaction.

Butanone ($CH_3COCH_2CH_3$) contains the $CH_3CO-$ moiety and undergoes haloform reaction.

Propanal ($CH_3CH_2CHO$) lacks the $CH_3CO-$ moiety, possessing instead $CH_3CH_2CO-$, and does not exhibit the haloform reaction.

The compound that does not undergo haloform reaction is therefore $\boxed{B}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is used as reagent in Etard reaction?
questions.solution:
In the Étard reaction, an aromatic or heterocyclic methyl group undergoes direct oxidation to an aldehyde using chromyl chloride ($\mathrm{CrO_2 Cl_2}$), proceeding through an intermediate chromyl ester that is hydrolyzed to yield the aldehyde product. For instance, toluene is converted to benzaldehyde:

$\mathrm{C_6 H_5-CH_3 \xrightarrow{CrO_2 Cl_2, CS_2} [C_6 H_5-CH(OCrOHCl_2)2] \xrightarrow{H_3 O^+} C_6 H_5-CHO}$

Chromyl chloride ($\mathrm{CrO_2 Cl_2}$) is the specific reagent employed.

Among the options, $\mathrm{CrCl_3}$ is incorrect; $\mathrm{CrO_3}$ and $\mathrm{H2CrO4}$ are oxidizing agents but typically lead to overoxidation to carboxylic acids rather than stopping at the aldehyde stage.

Final answer: $\boxed{B}$

Among the choices: Option A describes this reaction correctly. Clemmensen reduction uses Zn(Hg) and HCl; the Stephen reaction converts nitriles to aldehydes; and the Étard reaction oxidizes methyl groups to aldehydes.

The transformation is achieved specifically by the Wolf-Kishner reduction.

Ethanal contains $\alpha$-hydrogens and undergoes aldol condensation under dilute NaOH. Two molecules react via aldol addition to form 3-hydroxybutanal:

The product sequence yields 3-hydroxybutanal (A) followed by but-2-enal (B). Among the options, but-2-enal corresponds to option C.

questions.q: Which from following compounds has highest boiling point?
questions.solution:
Boiling points in organic compounds are governed by intermolecular force strength. Among homologous aldehyde series, increasing molecular weight and chain length enhance London dispersion interactions.

Molecular weights are calculated as follows: acetaldehyde (C2H4O) $\mathrm{MW} = 44.06$ g/mol, propionaldehyde (C3H6O) $\mathrm{MW} = 58.09$ g/mol, butyraldehyde (C4H8O) $\mathrm{MW} = 72.12$ g/mol, and valeraldehyde (C5H10O) $\mathrm{MW} = 86.15$ g/mol.

Valeraldehyde possesses the greatest molecular mass and longest carbon chain, resulting in the most substantial London dispersion forces. These stronger interactions necessitate higher energy input for phase transition, correlating with an elevated boiling point.

Answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

questions.q: Which from following reagents is used in Gatterman-Koch formylation of arene?
questions.solution:
The Gatterman-Koch reaction is a Friedel-Crafts acylation that formylates aromatic rings using carbon monoxide and hydrogen chloride with anhydrous aluminum chloride catalysis.

Carbon monoxide and hydrogen chloride combine with $\mathrm{AlCl}_3$ to generate the formyl cation electrophile: $\mathrm{CO} + \mathrm{HCl} + \mathrm{AlCl}_3 \rightleftharpoons [\mathrm{HCO}^+]\mathrm{AlCl}_4^-$. This species undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution, attacking the ring and forming an arenium ion intermediate that deprotonates to yield the aldehyde product.

Option A ($\mathrm{AlH}(i-\mathrm{Bu})_2$) and D (DIBAL-H) are reducing agents, not formylation reagents. Option C ($\mathrm{CrO}_2\mathrm{Cl}_2$ in $\mathrm{CS}_2$) is used for methyl group oxidation in the Etard reaction. Only option B ($\mathrm{CO}, \mathrm{HCl}$ with anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl}_3$) provides the correct reagents.

The reagents are therefore identified as $\boxed{\text{B}}$.

questions.solution:

The final answer is $\boxed{\text{B}}$.
